chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about a woman who had a husband who refused to give her permission to perform Hajj, and she had not yet performed the Hajj of Islam. So her husband was absent from her, and he had forbidden her to perform Hajj. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no obedience to him upon her regarding the Hajj of Islam, so let her perform Hajj if she wishes.'

key_terms.حَجَّةُ الْإِسْلَامِ: The first obligatory pilgrimage to Mecca
key_terms.طَاعَة: Obedience (specifically spousal obedience in this context)

ai.seo_question: Can a woman perform her obligatory Hajj if her husband forbids it?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the husband's authority to withhold permission does not override the woman's individual obligation of Hajjat al-Islam, distinguishing it from other acts requiring consent. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that while marital harmony is valued, the fulfillment of a direct divine command remains independent of the husband's veto, allowing her to proceed even in his absence. It highlights the balance between marital rights and individual religious duties in Shia fiqh.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a woman who had a husband for her who refused to allow her that she should perform Hajj, and she had not performed the Hajj of Al-Islam. So the husband was absent from her, and he had forbidden her to perform Hajj. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no obedience to him upon her with regards to Hajj of Al-Islam, so let her perform Hajj if she so desires it’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Ali ibn abu Hamzah who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a woman whose husband refuses to permit her to perform al-Hajj and she has not performed Hajjahta al-Islam. The husband who had prohibited her to perform Hajjahta al-Islam disappeared. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not obligatory for her to obey him in his prohibiting from Hajjahta al-Islam. She can perform al-Hajj whenever she likes.’”
